newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese watch firms clock up higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Japanese watch firms clock up higher profits.

text.p: Japan's two leading watch companies reported a surge in their interim profits Tuesday, citing cost-cutting and the yen's decline against the dollar.

Seiko Corp. said its parent current profit for the first half of the 1996/97 business year jumped almost 17-fold from a year ago to 1.15 billion yen ($10.3 million). However, sales fell 6.7 percent to 101.3 billion yen ($913 million).
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks.
Seiko produces wrist watches and jewelry, and its group firms make high-end timepieces.

Another major watchmaker, Citizen Watch Co. Ltd., also saw profits surge. It reported a 40 percent rise for the six-month period to 5.9 billion yen ($53.1 million), despite a 6.8 percent drop in sales to 100.4 billion yen ($904 million).

A yen decline against the dollar helps increase yen-denominated income and overseas sales. The yen has retreated sharply from postwar highs hit last year, and was trading at around 111 yen Tuesday compared with a post-war high of 79.75 in April 1995.
"We were able to increase overseas sales significantly partly as a result of the yen's decline," a Seiko spokesman said.
The company said that the decline in its sales was mainly due to its shifting of its money-losing domestic business in clocks to a subsidiary in July.
For the full year, Seiko expects to post 192 billion yen ($1.72 billion) in sales and 2.5 billion yen ($22.5 million) in parent current profit.
At Citizen, sales of wrist watches, the company's main product line, increased, but sales of information equipment and parts, including notebook personal computers, fell.
The company moved some production operations overseas. It also placed emphasis on making more profitable models of printers than its mainstay dot-matrix printers.
